claims.text: The baseline refractory high-entropy alloy has a relatively coarse grain structure.
The baseline alloy has no engineered nanoscale reinforcement.
Adding nanoscale Y2O3 by powder metallurgy or a similar route can produce a controlled oxide dispersion in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The intervention can produce uniformly distributed nanoscale Y2O3 particles at grain boundaries.
The intervention can produce uniformly distributed nanoscale Y2O3 particles throughout the alloy matrix.
Nanoscale oxide dispersoids inhibit dislocation motion.
Nanoscale oxide dispersoids pin grain boundaries.
Nanoscale oxide dispersoids serve as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Dislocation pinning by the oxide dispersoids increases yield strength.
Dislocation and grain-boundary pinning by the oxide dispersoids improves creep resistance.
Defect-sink behavior of the oxide dispersoids mitigates irradiation-induced defects.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will have greater yield strength than the alloy without oxide dispersoids.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will have greater tensile strength than the alloy without oxide dispersoids.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will have better creep resistance than the alloy without oxide dispersoids.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will maintain phase stability during combined high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
The oxide-dispersed alloy will maintain microstructural stability during combined high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
Mechanical improvement depends on retaining a fine, uniform dispersion of oxide particles.
Coarsening or agglomeration of the oxide dispersoids under extreme conditions may diminish their mechanical benefits.
